---
title: "Descriptive statistics"
---

These ten functions summarize ordinary PHP numeric arrays. They are deterministic,
stateless native calculations; no intercept, model fitting or retained sample
object is involved. Array keys are ignored and iteration order aligns pairs and
weights. Results are floats except `stat_quantile_array`, which returns a packed
list in probability-array iteration order.

## Calls and conventions

```php
Phit\stat_mean(array $values, string $missing = 'raise'): float;
Phit\stat_var(array $values, string $type = 'sample', string $missing = 'raise'): float;
Phit\stat_sd(array $values, string $type = 'sample', string $missing = 'raise'): float;
Phit\stat_cov(array $x, array $y, string $type = 'sample', string $missing = 'raise'): float;
Phit\stat_cor(array $x, array $y, string $missing = 'raise'): float;
Phit\stat_quantile(array $values, float $p, string $missing = 'raise'): float;
Phit\stat_quantile_array(array $values, array $probabilities, string $missing = 'raise'): array;
Phit\stat_median(array $values, string $missing = 'raise'): float;
Phit\stat_weighted_mean(array $values, array $weights, string $missing = 'raise'): float;
Phit\stat_weighted_var(array $values, array $weights, string $type = 'frequency', string $missing = 'raise'): float;
```

`type: 'sample'` variance/SD/covariance divides by n−1; `'population'` divides by n.
Population variance/SD permits one value and returns zero. Covariance/correlation
requires at least two aligned retained pairs under either normalization. Other
summaries require one retained value. Correlation with a constant input is NAN,
an explicitly undefined statistic. An empty requested probability array returns
`[]` after validating the supplied values.

Quantiles use R's default **type 7** interpolation. For sorted values x, index
$h=1+(n-1)p$; interpolate between adjacent values using the fractional part of h.
p must be in `[0,1]`. Endpoints are the minimum and maximum. Median is the type-7
quantile at p=0.5. The batch function sorts once for all requested probabilities;
it returns exactly the same values as scalar calls.

## Weight definitions

Let $W=\sum_i w_i$, $m=\sum_i w_i x_i/W$, and $SS=\sum_i w_i(x_i-m)^2$.
Weights must be nonnegative and finite; the retained total must be positive.

| Weighted variance type | Definition | Interpretation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `frequency` (default) | $SS/(W-1)$ | Replication/count weights; requires W > 1 |
| `reliability` | $SS/(W-\sum_i w_i^2/W)$ | Reliability/precision weights; requires a positive denominator |
| `population` | $SS/W$ | Weighted population second moment |

Frequency and reliability weighting differ. Integer frequency weights reproduce
the sample variance of an expanded sample. Reliability/population results are
invariant to multiplying all weights by a positive constant. Zero weights are
allowed. One effective value has zero population variance but undefined reliability
variance. Negative weights are rejected even when the paired value is missing.
Weights are aligned to original input positions before pairwise deletion.
The separate [draw moments](draw-numerics.qmd) API always normalizes weights and
calls reliability normalization `'unbiased'`; it never treats weights as counts.

## Missing values and errors

Null and NAN are missing values. The default `missing: 'raise'` rejects them with
1001. `missing: 'drop'` explicitly removes them, **pairwise** for covariance,
correlation and weighted functions. No warning or retained-row metadata is returned;
dropping is opt-in. Infinity always raises 1003, including an element paired with
a missing value. Strings, booleans, objects and nested arrays raise 1001. All
aligned arrays must have equal original lengths, or 1002 is raised.

Unsupported type/missing options, insufficient retained values, invalid weights
or invalid probability domains raise 1001. NAN probability raises 1003. Nonfinite
arithmetic results also raise 1003, including an overflowing weight sum or squared
deviation. The explicit NAN for constant-input correlation remains valid. This
release fixed a case where an overflowing variance had been hidden as zero by
floating-point `max(NAN, 0)`.

Sums use Neumaier compensation; variances/covariances use corrected two-pass
centered moments. This improves accuracy with large common offsets. These are
binary64 calculations and do not promise arbitrary-scale extended precision.

## Example and verification

```php
$values = [2.5, 3.1, 4.7, 1.2, 9.8, 5.5, 3.3];
$mean = Phit\stat_mean($values);                     // 4.3
$sampleVariance = Phit\stat_var($values);       // About 7.85667
$quartiles = Phit\stat_quantile_array($values, [.25, .5, .75]);
$explicitDrop = Phit\stat_mean([1, null, 3], missing: 'drop'); // 2
```

`tests/descriptive.php` checks 145 R reference quantities plus scalar/batch
consistency, missing policies, pairwise deletion, weights, boundaries, malformed
inputs and arithmetic overflow. `crates/stats-core/tests/descriptive.rs` checks
the same stored R cases independently of PHP and adds core failure/degeneracy
checks. The eight univariate samples, three paired samples and two weighted samples
include large offsets, tiny values, constant data and reproducible simulations.
Reference tolerance is relative `1e-12`, with exact zeros. R is not required by
the ordinary test suites.

Regenerate intentionally with `Rscript tests/generate-distribution-fixtures.R`;
this also regenerates the distribution R fixture. The [provenance manifest](verifications/reference-manifest.json)
records inputs, versions, generators and hashes. The [release gate](verification.qmd)
includes the PHP suite and the runnable `examples/distributions.php`.
